findings.failure_mode: Corrupted or missing file silently panics the caller instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: Return a Result<Record, FrameError> or similar typed error; use map_err or ? to propagate IOError as a domain error

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() — unwrap on parse of untrusted field
findings.failure_mode: Non-numeric value in field 1 panics the caller instead of returning a typed ParseError
findings.fix: Replace with parts[1].parse::<u16>().map_err(|e| ParseError::Value(e)) or similar typed error path

findings.problem: Lossy `as u16` cast after parse — truncated range, silently wraps or truncates values >65535
findings.failure_mode: A valid u32 value in range 65536..=4294967295 silently truncates to u16, producing incorrect data with no error
findings.fix: Parse directly as u16 via `.parse::<u16>()`, or use `u16::try_from(val)` and map overflow to a typed OverflowError

findings.problem: parts[0] — unchecked indexing into split result
findings.failure_mode: A line with zero comma-separated fields panics via IndexOutOfBounds
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and match on (name, value) Option, or use get(0) and map_err to a MalformedLineError

findings.problem: parts[1] — unchecked indexing into split result
findings.failure_mode: A line with only one comma-separated field panics via IndexOutOfBounds
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and handle the missing second field as a MalformedLineError

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) — I/O side effect inside data-loading function
findings.failure_mode: Purity is broken: the function has a hidden stdout side effect, making it non-deterministic, untestable in isolation, and unusable in contexts where stdout is captured or redirected
findings.fix: Remove println! entirely from the parsing pipeline. If logging is needed, return a separate log/result struct or push logs through an explicit callback/lifecycle in the imperative shell

findings.problem: Vec::collect() from split without try_reserve or capacity bounds
findings.failure_mode: A single line with an enormous number of commas triggers unbounded allocation, potentially OOM
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') for single-separator parsing, or use try_reserve on the Vec with a documented per-line cap, returning Allocation error on failure

findings.problem: load_frames returns Vec<Record> with no error type — all failures are panics
findings.failure_mode: Every failure mode (IO, parse, index, overflow) collapses into a panic, making error handling impossible for callers
findings.fix: Change signature to `pub fn load_frames(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, FrameError>` and define a typed FrameError enum (Io, Parse, MalformedLine, Overflow, Allocation)

findings.problem: No benchmark exists for load_frames throughput or latency
findings.failure_mode: Any performance claim about this parser is ungrounded; regressions in allocation or parsing speed are undetectable
findings.fix: Add a criterion or custom benchmark measuring lines-per-second and per-line allocation count for typical and adversarial input sizes

findings.problem: No profiler evidence (flamegraph, perf, or similar) for hot-path allocation profile
findings.failure_mode: Intermediate Vec/String allocations per line cannot be proven unnecessary; Cow or pre-borrowed patterns may be beneficial but are unmeasured
findings.fix: Run flamegraph or perf record on representative input; use &str and split_once to avoid per-field String allocation if profiler shows it matters

no typed error taxonomy defined for the domain
residual_risk: This crate has 8 blockers and 2 warnings. Every public error path is a panic via unwrap or unchecked indexing. The function mixes I/O (fs::read_to_string, println!) with data parsing, violating the functional core / imperative shell boundary. Even a minimal fix would require: (1) adding a typed FrameError enum, (2) changing load_frames to return Result<Vec<Record>, FrameError>, (3) replacing all unwrap() calls with ?/map_err, (4) replacing parts[0]/parts[1] indexing with split_once, (5) replacing `as u16` with checked conversion, (6) removing println! from the parsing pipeline. Without benchmarks or profiler data, performance characteristics of the fixed implementation are unproven. Static review only; no commands were run.
